title: Nginx 502 Bad Gateway
facts: A 502 response means Nginx could not obtain a valid response from the configured upstream.
Possible causes include an unavailable upstream process, a wrong upstream address or port, or a local network/socket issue.
A 502 by itself does not prove that the database or application code is faulty.
read_only_checks: Inspect recent Nginx error-log entries for the failing upstream address and port.
Read the upstream service status and recent journal logs without changing service state.
Compare the configured upstream host/port with the actual listener configuration.
escalation_notes: Escalate when the upstream is unavailable across multiple checks or when recovery requires a service restart or deployment.

title: PostgreSQL connection pool saturation
facts: Pool acquisition timeouts can occur when the application exhausts its configured connection pool.
Database-wide connection pressure and application pool saturation are related but distinct signals.
Increasing pool size without checking database connection limits and replica count can make saturation worse.
read_only_checks: Inspect current and maximum PostgreSQL connection counts using read-only statistics views.
Review application pool-acquisition timeout metrics and pool in-use/idle gauges.
Compare replica count multiplied by maximum pool size with the configured database connection limit.
escalation_notes: Escalate before changing pool limits, database settings or replica count.

title: DNS resolution and TLS certificate validation
facts: A DNS failure prevents the client from resolving the service hostname to an address.
TLS validation can fail when a certificate is expired, not yet valid, untrusted or does not cover the requested hostname.
DNS resolution and certificate validation should be checked separately.
read_only_checks: Inspect DNS A/AAAA and CNAME resolution from the affected runtime environment.
Inspect certificate subject, issuer, SAN hostnames and validity dates without sending credentials.
Compare the requested hostname with the certificate SAN list.
escalation_notes: Escalate before changing DNS records, certificates, trust stores or network policy.

title: Kubernetes container restart investigation
facts: Repeated container restarts can be caused by process crashes, failed probes, resource limits or dependency failures.
An OOMKilled status indicates the container was terminated after exceeding its memory limit.
A restart count alone is insufficient to establish root cause; termination reason and previous-container logs are needed.
read_only_checks: Inspect pod status, restart count, termination reason and last exit code.
Read previous-container logs and recent namespace events.
Compare observed memory usage with the configured container memory limit.
escalation_notes: Escalate before editing a workload, changing resource limits or deleting/restarting a pod.
